chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the man who rests during his Tawaf.
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. I used to have an enclosure placed for me, so I would sit upon it.'

key_terms.مِرْفَقَةٌ: An enclosure or seat for resting

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sit or rest during Tawaf if one is tired?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the principle of *rukhas* (concessions) in Shia jurisprudence, demonstrating that the validity of Tawaf is not compromised by necessary pauses for fatigue. The Imam’s personal practice of using a dedicated seat (*mirfaka*) serves as a normative precedent (*sunna*) for worshippers, emphasizing that the ritual remains continuous even when physical comfort requires temporary interruption.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having been asked about the man who rests during his Tawaaf.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. I<sup>asws</sup> had been such, so an enclosure was set up for me, so I<sup>asws</sup> sat upon it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from ibn abu Ya’fur who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about a man who rests during his Tawaf.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so. For me a resting arrangement was made so I could sit on it to rest.’”
